title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Corinthians chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Corinthians Chapter 1.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 1, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ
Grace be to you and peace
Who comforteth us in all our tribulation
questions.correctAnswer: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: The first mention in the chapter is 'Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ' found in 2 Corinthians 1:1.

questions.question: Who is mentioned as the brother of Paul in the greeting?
questions.correctAnswer: Timothy
questions.explanation: Timothy is mentioned as 'our brother' in 2 Corinthians 1:1.

questions.question: To whom is the letter addressed?
options: The church of God in Ephesus
The church of God which is at Corinth
The church of God in Jerusalem
The church of God in Rome
questions.correctAnswer: The church of God which is at Corinth
questions.explanation: The letter is addressed 'unto the church of God which is at Corinth' as stated in 2 Corinthians 1:1.

questions.question: What does Paul wish for the recipients in 2 Corinthians 1:2?
questions.correctAnswer: Grace and peace
questions.explanation: Paul wishes 'Grace be to you and peace' in 2 Corinthians 1:2.

questions.question: Who is referred to as 'the Father of mercies'?
questions.correctAnswer: God
questions.explanation: 'Blessed be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies' is stated in 2 Corinthians 1:3.

questions.question: What is God described as in 2 Corinthians 1:3?
options: The Creator of heaven and earth
questions.correctAnswer: The God of all comfort
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 1:3, God is referred to as 'the God of all comfort'.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 1:4, why does God comfort us?
options: So we can ignore our tribulations
So we may be able to comfort others
questions.correctAnswer: So we may be able to comfort others
questions.explanation: The verse states that God comforts us 'that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble' as per 2 Corinthians 1:4.

questions.question: What abounds in us according to 2 Corinthians 1:5?
questions.correctAnswer: The sufferings of Christ
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us' in 2 Corinthians 1:5.

questions.question: What is the purpose of our afflictions according to 2 Corinthians 1:6?
questions.correctAnswer: For your consolation and salvation
questions.explanation: The purpose of afflictions is stated as 'it is for your consolation and salvation' in 2 Corinthians 1:6.

questions.question: What is said about hope in 2 Corinthians 1:7?
questions.correctAnswer: It is stedfast
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'And our hope of you is stedfast' in 2 Corinthians 1:7.

questions.question: What trouble did Paul mention in 2 Corinthians 1:8?
questions.correctAnswer: Trouble in Asia
questions.explanation: Paul mentions 'our trouble which came to us in Asia' in 2 Corinthians 1:8.

questions.question: True or False: Paul was an apostle by the will of God.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Paul is described as 'an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God' in 2 Corinthians 1:1.

questions.question: True or False: The God of all comfort comforts us in our tribulations.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'Who comforteth us in all our tribulation' in 2 Corinthians 1:4.

questions.question: True or False: Paul was never despaired of life.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 1:8, Paul indicates they 'despaired even of life'.

questions.question: True or False: Timothy was the only one mentioned in the greeting.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The greeting includes both Paul and Timothy as stated in 2 Corinthians 1:1.

medium.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Corinthians Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 1:9, why did Paul say they had the sentence of death in themselves?
options: So that they would trust in God who raises the dead
Because they had committed a grave sin
To prove their courage in the face of death
To fulfill a prophecy about suffering
questions.correctAnswer: So that they would trust in God who raises the dead
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:9 states that they had the sentence of death so that they should not trust in themselves, but in God who raises the dead.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 1:11 promise will happen if the Corinthians help together by prayer for Paul and his companions?
options: Thanks will be given by many on their behalf
They will be delivered from trouble
questions.correctAnswer: Thanks will be given by many on their behalf
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:11 says that by helping together through prayer, thanks may be given by many on their behalf.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 1:10, what is the nature of God’s deliverance?
options: God delivered them from great death, does deliver, and will yet deliver
God delivered them once but will not deliver again
God’s deliverance is only for spiritual death
God’s deliverance is a future promise only
questions.correctAnswer: God delivered them from great death, does deliver, and will yet deliver
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:10 emphasizes that God delivered them from great death, does deliver, and they trust He will yet deliver them.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 1:15 connect with 1:16 in terms of Paul's travel plans?
options: Paul planned to visit the Corinthians before going to Macedonia and return through Macedonia
Paul planned to stay in Corinth and not travel
Paul intended to go directly to Judaea from Macedonia without visiting Corinth again
Paul wanted to avoid Macedonia entirely
questions.correctAnswer: Paul planned to visit the Corinthians before going to Macedonia and return through Macedonia
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:15-16 describe Paul's intention to come to the Corinthians first, then pass into Macedonia, and afterward return to the Corinthians on his way to Judaea.

questions.question: What attitude does Paul emphasize in 2 Corinthians 1:12 regarding his conduct in the world?
options: Simplicity and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Simplicity and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:12 states Paul’s conduct is marked by simplicity and godly sincerity, not fleshly wisdom but by the grace of God.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 1:14, what mutual relationship do Paul and the Corinthians share?
options: They are each other's rejoicing in the day of the Lord Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: They are each other's rejoicing in the day of the Lord Jesus
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:14 explains that Paul and the Corinthians acknowledge each other as their rejoicing in the day of the Lord Jesus.

questions.question: What role does prayer play according to 2 Corinthians 1:11 in the lives of Paul and his companions?
options: Prayer helps together so that thanks may be given for the gift bestowed
Prayer is a private matter with no effect on others
Prayer is only for personal gain
Prayer is unnecessary because of God’s sovereignty
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer helps together so that thanks may be given for the gift bestowed
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:11 highlights that the Corinthians’ united prayers help so that many may give thanks for the gift bestowed upon Paul and his companions.

questions.question: What does Paul mean by 'our conversation in the world' in 2 Corinthians 1:12?
options: Our conduct or way of life
questions.correctAnswer: Our conduct or way of life
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 1:12, 'conversation' refers to conduct or manner of life lived in simplicity and godly sincerity.

questions.question: How does Paul describe the motive behind his writings to the Corinthians in 2 Corinthians 1:13?
options: He writes only what they have read or acknowledged
He writes new revelations for them
He writes to confuse his opponents
He writes to change their beliefs
questions.correctAnswer: He writes only what they have read or acknowledged
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:13 states that Paul writes nothing other than what the Corinthians have already read or acknowledged.

questions.question: What hope does Paul express for the Corinthians in 2 Corinthians 1:14?
options: That they will continue to be his rejoicing as he is theirs
That they will forget his teachings
questions.correctAnswer: That they will continue to be his rejoicing as he is theirs
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:14 expresses Paul’s hope that the Corinthians will continue to be his rejoicing as he is theirs on the day of the Lord Jesus.

questions.question: What was the purpose of Paul’s intended visit to the Corinthians before going to Macedonia according to 2 Corinthians 1:15?
options: That they might have a second benefit
questions.correctAnswer: That they might have a second benefit
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:15 reveals Paul’s intention to visit to provide the Corinthians with a second benefit.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 1:9 teach practical Christian living about trust?
options: Do not trust in yourself but in God who raises the dead
Trust only in your own strength
questions.correctAnswer: Do not trust in yourself but in God who raises the dead
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:9 instructs believers to trust not in themselves but in God who raises the dead, emphasizing reliance on divine power.

questions.question: What does Paul say about suffering and consolation in the earlier context of 2 Corinthians 1:5?
options: As the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also aboundeth by Christ
Suffering should be avoided at all costs
Consolation comes only after suffering ends
questions.correctAnswer: As the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also aboundeth by Christ
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:5 teaches that our sufferings, like those of Christ, are accompanied by abundant consolation through Christ.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Corinthians 1:12, Paul claims to use fleshly wisdom in his conduct toward the Corinthians.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:12 explicitly states Paul does not act with fleshly wisdom but by the grace of God.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Corinthians 1:10 indicates that God does not deliver believers from death.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:10 affirms that God delivered them from great death, does deliver, and will yet deliver them.

hard.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Corinthians Chapter 1.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 1:17, what rhetorical question does Paul ask to emphasize his sincerity in purpose?
questions.correctAnswer: Did I use lightness?
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 1:17, Paul asks, 'did I use lightness?' to emphasize that his intentions were serious and sincere.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 1:18, how does Paul describe God's truthfulness in relation to their word?
options: Our word toward you was not yea and nay
Our messages were full of doubt
questions.correctAnswer: Our word toward you was not yea and nay
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:18 states, 'But as God is true, our word toward you was not yea and nay,' emphasizing consistency and truthfulness.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 1:19, who are identified as the preachers of Jesus Christ among the Corinthians?
questions.correctAnswer: Paul, Silvanus, and Timotheus
questions.explanation: Verse 19 identifies 'me and Silvanus and Timotheus' as those who preached Jesus Christ among the Corinthians.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 1:20 say about the promises of God in Christ?
options: All the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen
The promises are conditional and uncertain
Some promises are yea, others are nay
questions.correctAnswer: All the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:20 affirms that 'all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen,' showing their certainty and fulfillment in Christ.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 1:21, who establishes and anoints the believers in Christ?
questions.correctAnswer: God
questions.explanation: Verse 21 states, 'Now he which stablisheth us with you in Christ, and hath anointed us, is God,' attributing the establishment and anointing to God.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 1:22, what has God given as a seal and earnest in believers' hearts?
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:22 says God 'hath also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts,' identifying the Spirit as the seal and earnest.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'epangelia' (ἐπαγγελία) in 2 Corinthians 1:20 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Promise
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'epangelia' in 2 Corinthians 1:20 means 'promise,' referring to God's assurances fulfilled in Christ.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 2 Corinthians 1:18-20 to emphasize God's faithfulness?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: These verses use an inclusio framing with 'not yea and nay' surrounding the affirmation of God's truthfulness, a literary device to emphasize reliability.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of God as the 'Father of mercies' in 2 Corinthians 1:3?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 63:9
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:9 refers to God as a merciful Father who delivers, resonating with 2 Corinthians 1:3's 'Father of mercies.'

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God comforting believers in their tribulations found in 2 Corinthians 1:4?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 8:28
questions.explanation: Romans 8:28 discusses God working all things for good to those who love Him, echoing the comfort in tribulations theme of 2 Corinthians 1:4.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Paul’s statement in 2 Corinthians 1:17 about purpose and lightness?
options: His plan to visit Corinth and Macedonia
An account of his affliction in Asia
A prayer request for the Corinthians
A greeting to the church in Corinth
questions.correctAnswer: His plan to visit Corinth and Macedonia
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:16 describes Paul’s travel plans, which immediately precede his reflection in verse 17 on his sincerity of purpose.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 1:9 illustrate a theological principle about trusting God rather than oneself?
options: It describes the sentence of death so believers trust in God who raises the dead
It commands believers to abandon hope
It teaches reliance on human wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: It describes the sentence of death so believers trust in God who raises the dead
questions.explanation: Verse 9 shows Paul and companions faced death to teach trust in God who raises the dead, highlighting reliance on divine power over self.

questions.question: What typology is illustrated in 2 Corinthians 1:10 with God delivering Paul from great death?
questions.correctAnswer: Christ as the ultimate Deliverer
questions.explanation: Paul's deliverance foreshadows Christ's ultimate deliverance of believers from death, a typological fulfillment discussed in 2 Corinthians 1:10.

questions.question: What foreshadowing is present in 2 Corinthians 1:23 regarding Paul's delayed visit to Corinth?
options: Paul spares the Corinthians temporarily to avoid causing grief
Paul plans to abandon the church
Paul intends to deliver a harsh rebuke
Paul is uncertain about his mission
questions.correctAnswer: Paul spares the Corinthians temporarily to avoid causing grief
questions.explanation: In verse 23, Paul calls God to witness that he delayed his visit to spare the Corinthians, foreshadowing a later visit with a different purpose.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 1:24, do Paul and his companions have dominion over the Corinthians' faith?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:24 explicitly states, 'Not for that we have dominion over your faith,' denying such authority.

theological.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Corinthians Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 1:3 teach about God’s nature?
options: God is the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort
God is a distant judge who punishes sin
God is primarily a creator concerned with natural order
God is unknowable and beyond human experience
questions.correctAnswer: God is the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:3 explicitly calls God the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort, emphasizing His merciful and comforting nature.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 1:9 teach about human trust and divine power?
options: Believers should trust in God who raises the dead rather than themselves
Human strength is sufficient for enduring trials without divine help
Faith in oneself is the ultimate source of hope
Death is the final end, and there is no resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: Believers should trust in God who raises the dead rather than themselves
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:9 teaches that the apostle and his companions learned not to trust in themselves but in God who raises the dead, highlighting the doctrine of reliance on divine resurrection power.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 1:20 teach regarding God's promises?
options: All the promises of God find their 'yes' and 'amen' in Christ
God’s promises are conditional and often uncertain
God’s promises are fulfilled only in the age to come
Promises of God can be broken by human unbelief
questions.correctAnswer: All the promises of God find their 'yes' and 'amen' in Christ
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:20 states that in Christ all the promises of God are affirmed ('yes') and guaranteed ('amen'), underscoring the fulfillment of divine promises in Jesus Christ.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 1:4 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Comforting mercy
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:4 highlights God's attribute of comforting mercy, as God comforts believers in their troubles so they might comfort others.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 1:22 specifically demonstrate?
options: Faithfulness in sealing believers with the Holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness in sealing believers with the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:22 shows God’s faithfulness in sealing believers and giving the earnest of the Spirit, marking them as His own.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 1:8-9 connect to the broader biblical theme of suffering and reliance on God?
options: It illustrates that believers endure suffering to learn dependence on God’s resurrection power
It teaches that suffering is evidence of God’s displeasure
It suggests believers should avoid suffering at all costs
It claims that suffering is meaningless in Christian life
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates that believers endure suffering to learn dependence on God’s resurrection power
questions.explanation: Verses 8-9 describe Paul’s experience of extreme suffering that led to despair of life, teaching that such trials are meant to turn believers away from self-trust to trust in God who raises the dead.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 1:15-17 anticipate the theme of integrity in Paul’s ministry later in the epistle?
options: Paul defends his sincere and consistent intentions against accusations of fickleness
Paul admits to changing plans frequently for convenience
Paul emphasizes that his ministry is guided by human wisdom
Paul ignores accusations regarding his travel plans
questions.correctAnswer: Paul defends his sincere and consistent intentions against accusations of fickleness
questions.explanation: In 1:15-17, Paul insists that his purposes are not 'yes and no' but consistent and sincere, setting the stage for his defense of apostolic integrity throughout the letter.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 3 and 4 teach about God’s role in suffering and comfort?
options: God is both merciful and the source of comfort that equips believers to comfort others
God causes suffering as punishment without offering comfort
God is distant and indifferent to human troubles
God comforts only the apostles, not the general church
questions.correctAnswer: God is both merciful and the source of comfort that equips believers to comfort others
questions.explanation: Verses 3 and 4 together portray God as 'Father of mercies' and the 'God of all comfort,' who comforts believers in tribulation so they can comfort others with the same comfort.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 20 and 21 teach about Christ’s role in the believer’s assurance?
options: Christ guarantees the fulfillment of all God’s promises and establishes believers in Him
Christ’s promises are uncertain and require human effort to fulfill
Believers must rely on their own works for assurance
Christ is only a model, not a guarantee of promises
questions.correctAnswer: Christ guarantees the fulfillment of all God’s promises and establishes believers in Him
questions.explanation: Verse 20 emphasizes that all God’s promises are 'yes' and 'amen' in Christ, and verse 21 states that God establishes believers with Christ, ensuring assurance in salvation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 6 and 7 teach about the shared experience of suffering and consolation in the church?
options: Sufferings and consolation are shared among believers, contributing to mutual salvation and hope
Suffering is individual and unrelated to the community
Consolation is reserved only for apostles
questions.correctAnswer: Sufferings and consolation are shared among believers, contributing to mutual salvation and hope
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 teach that whether Paul and his companions are afflicted or comforted, it is for the Corinthians’ consolation and salvation, showing the communal nature of suffering and comfort.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Paul’s change of travel plans indicates he was unreliable and acted according to fleshly desires. What does 2 Corinthians 1:15-18 actually teach?
options: Paul’s intentions were sincere and consistent, guided by God’s truth, not by human fickleness
Paul frequently changed plans to please different groups
Paul admitted to acting impulsively without reflection
Paul’s travel was dictated by political convenience
questions.correctAnswer: Paul’s intentions were sincere and consistent, guided by God’s truth, not by human fickleness
questions.explanation: Verses 15-18 clarify that Paul’s plans were not 'yes and no' but consistent and truthful, reflecting sincerity and divine guidance rather than human fickleness.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 1:24 teach about the apostles’ relation to believers’ faith?
options: Apostles do not have dominion over believers’ faith but are helpers of their joy
Apostles control the faith of believers authoritatively
Believers’ faith depends entirely on apostolic power
Faith is unnecessary because apostles have dominion
questions.correctAnswer: Apostles do not have dominion over believers’ faith but are helpers of their joy
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:24 states apostles are not rulers over others’ faith but helpers of their joy, emphasizing servant leadership rather than domination.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 1:10 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Deliverance and ongoing salvation
questions.explanation: Verse 10 highlights God’s attribute of deliverance, having saved Paul and continuing to save, showing God’s ongoing saving power.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 1:12-14 contribute to the theme of apostolic integrity and mutual joy in the church?
options: Apostles live with simplicity and godly sincerity, rejoicing mutually with the church
Apostles manipulate the church for personal gain
Mutual joy is irrelevant to apostolic ministry
Apostles boast in worldly wisdom rather than grace
questions.correctAnswer: Apostles live with simplicity and godly sincerity, rejoicing mutually with the church
questions.explanation: Verses 12-14 emphasize the apostles’ sincere conduct and mutual rejoicing with the church, underscoring integrity and spiritual fellowship.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Corinthians 1:21-22 teach about God’s work in the believer’s sanctification?
options: God establishes, anoints, seals believers, and gives the Spirit as a guarantee
Believers sanctify themselves apart from God’s work
Sanctification is only a human effort
The Spirit is given only after final glorification
questions.correctAnswer: God establishes, anoints, seals believers, and gives the Spirit as a guarantee
questions.explanation: Verses 21-22 describe God’s active role in establishing, anointing, sealing believers and giving the Spirit as a down payment, teaching divine involvement in sanctification.
